dict.string: Play local audio files and browse tracks from folders using native file-opening integration.
Run the project and drop compatible audio files into the preview. Media files are not bundled with this example. Export the app to open tracks directly from Finder.
Choose Run, then Start Camera. Allow camera access when WebKit and macOS ask. Connect a camera to capture stills. Export App creates a separate app with its own camera permission.
A camera viewer with still capture, mirroring, frame guides, and image export.

Run to explore the interface without accessing your camera. Choose Export App, keep Camera Access enabled, then export and open the app bundle. Connect a camera and allow access when the exported app asks. The workspace preview explains these steps and does not request camera access.
Arrange pictures and filenames on a single PNG sheet.
Try the sample prints, change the columns, then save a PNG or drop your own folder.
Preview changes to a CSV and save a clean copy.
Compare the sample rows, choose what to clean, then save a new file.
Rehearse a talk one cue at a time, present on multiple displays, and share an editable, self-contained deck.

Edit a few cues, then choose Present. Use the arrow keys to advance and Escape to finish. Save Portable Deck creates a .htmltoapp file. Open it in HTML to App to convert the deck with its cues and icon intact.
A round analog clock that shows the same local time in its window and on its Dock icon.
Drag the face to move the clock. Press Escape for window controls. Export with a visible Dock icon to see both clocks run together.
Keep your favorite apps in a strip of clickable icons along any display edge.

Choose apps for your shelf, then pin it to a display edge. Try a shortcut in Preview and confirm which app to open. The project recommends separate permissions for listing and opening apps when you export.
Explore an illustrated bird guide stored as local JSON.
Search for a bird. Edit birds.json and reload to see your changes.
Run a focus timer and see the remaining minutes and seconds on the exported app's Dock icon.
Start a session in Preview. Choose Export App with a visible Dock icon, then turn on Dock progress. You can also let a Dock click pause or resume the timer.
Explore a folder and preview its images, audio, video, and text files through the local file bridge.
Run the project and drop a folder into the preview. Export the app to open folders directly from Finder.
Draw lines, shapes, arrows, and labels on a blank canvas or an image. Export your composition as a PNG.
Run the project and draw on the canvas. Drop an image into the preview to annotate it, then use Export PNG to save a copy.
Match pairs using sample artwork or installed app icons.
Turn over two cards. Try your app icons with listing access. No app is launched.
Browse images from a file or folder with a focused image viewer and native launch-item support.
Run the project and drop images or an image folder into the preview. Export the app to register the supported image formats with Finder.
Experiment with a native menu bar item, menus, badges, window titles, and window visibility.
Run the project to try the native controls. The demo can add a menu bar item while its preview is open. Close the preview to remove it. Test launch and close-to-menu-bar behavior in an exported app.
Send native notifications and update the Dock badge from JavaScript.

Run to explore the interface without requesting notification permission for HTML to App. Notifications and Dock badges are available after export. Choose Export App, open the exported app bundle, and request notification permission there. macOS notification settings may affect delivery.
Measure a layout with two graduated arms. The clear center lets you work with the window underneath.

Choose a size, display, and window level, then place the ruler. Drag either arm or use arrow keys to nudge it. Hold Shift to resize. Edit returns to setup. Share Project keeps its separate artwork, stylesheet, and script together.
Adjust subtitle timing and save a corrected SRT copy.
Play the sample and move the captions one second earlier to match the colors.
A text editor that demonstrates reading, editing, and saving local files through the native file bridge.

Run the project and drop a text file or folder into the preview. Work with a disposable copy when testing Save, because it changes the opened file. Export the app to use it with Finder's Open With menu.
Float a reference image over another app for tracing.
Float the sample, adjust its opacity, then lock it. Unlock it from the menu bar.
Play local movies in a dedicated viewer with support for files and folders opened from Finder.
Run the project and drop an MP4, MOV, or M4V file into the preview. Media files are not bundled with this example. Playback depends on the codecs supported by macOS.
